subject: On-prem control plane: SAML failover & SCIM incremental provisioning review
messages:
From: Andrew Miller <andrew.miller@nimbushealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rebecca Chan <rebecca.chan@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integrating our IdP with your on-prem control plane — questions on failover and provisioning

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We got good buy-in from our infra and security leads. A couple of follow-ups they asked me to put into one thread so we can plan the next steps: 

1) IdP failover: we run a geo-redundant ADFS + Okta combo with health checks. If the primary IdP is down, we'd like the control plane to accept assertions from a secondary provider without manual intervention. How do you recommend we configure SAML so we don't have to change SP metadata during a failover?

2) SCIM provisioning cadence: we prefer incremental deltas (add/update/remove) every 5 minutes from our SCIM gateway. Is Redwood's private control plane robust to high-frequency deltas? Any rate limits or dedupe behavior we should plan around?

3) Operator roles & emergency access: we need a documented fallback for an operator role (break-glass) that can be scoped tightly and audited. Should that be a SAML group claim or a SCIM role mapping?

Can we schedule a 45-min session next week to work through topology and mapping? I'm including Rebecca from our platform team.

Thanks,
Andrew

--
Andrew Miller
Director of Platform Engineering, Nimbus Health
andrew.miller@nimbushealth.com
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Miller <andrew.miller@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Rebecca Chan <rebecca.chan@nimbushealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integrating our IdP with your on-prem control plane — questions on failover and provisioning

Hi Andrew — thanks for consolidating. Happy to take these one at a time in a design session. Quick answers up front so your team can prep: 

- SAML failover: we can accept signed assertions from multiple issuers if you publish all IdP metadata to the SP trust store up front. The trick is handling NameID/subject collisions and audience restrictions — we usually recommend a short-lived assertion window (<=5m) plus an assertion "issuer_alias" claim to map to internal identity. See caveats below.

- SCIM deltas at 5m cadence: our Private control plane supports incremental provisioning. We perform idempotency checks and maintain a per-tenant change cursor; 5m is fine but we'll want to confirm peak churn rates (users created/updated/minute) so batching/dedupe can be tuned.

- Break-glass operator role: best practice is a dedicated service account (SCIM-provisioned) with MFA enforced and policy-bound roles. We do recommend recording the initial assignment via SCIM and mapping to an internally audited role. If you need just-in-time assertion-based elevation, SAML group-claim is workable but harder to audit retroactively.

I'll set up a technical design call. Proposed attendees: Vivek (runtime/authz), Dev (security/keys), Naomi (CS onboarding). Attached a rough failover topology and a proposed operator-role doc.

-Steph

Attachments: saml-failover-topology.png, operator-roles-proposal.md

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Andrew Miller <andrew.miller@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integrating our IdP with your on-prem control plane — questions on failover and provisioning

+1 to Steph's summary. A few implementation notes from runtime side: 

- Multiple IdP issuers: our SP implementation supports an array of trusted issuers. We map issuer -> tenant identity pool. During failover, the SP will accept assertions from any trusted issuer if the signature and audience checks pass. However, if two issuers assert the same external subject (same NameID), we need a deterministic tie-breaker. We prefer canonicalizing on issuer_alias claim rather than NameID alone.

- Cert rotation: make sure both primary and secondary IdPs publish current cert thumbprints. If you rotate certs frequently, add overlapping validity windows to avoid transient rejects.

- SCIM delta semantics: we recommend including an incremental cursor header (X-SCIM-Cursor) and UUID-based operation ids to avoid re-applying identical deltas. We will run deltas in a single-threaded apply loop per-tenant to avoid race conditions but can parallelize across tenants.

I'll bring a sketch of the idempotency layer to the call.

-Vivek
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Miller <andrew.miller@nimbushealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integrating our IdP with your on-prem control plane — questions on failover and provisioning

Andrew / Rebecca,

Thanks — some security-specific constraints to highlight before the design call: 

1) Metadata management: we require that all IdP metadata updates (new issuer, cert rotations) be submitted via the private control plane UI or API and scoped to the tenant. We do not support automatic metadata ingestion via email for private deployments (audit requirement).

2) Emergency access / break-glass: for private deployments we insist the break-glass account is provisioned as a scoped service principal with keys stored in your KMS. Redwood will insist on time-limited tokens for the operator role and will log role elevation events to the audit stream. We'll provide a runbook for manual activation (signed approval flow) if automated SAML elevation is unavailable.

3) SCIM throttling & backpressure: we implement token bucket rate-limiting per-tenant for SCIM writes. Default limits allow bursts equivalent to ~60 operations/minute per-tenant; we can raise that for enterprise contracts but need advance notice. We also expose retry-after headers for backpressure.

Please make sure platform ops are comfortable with signed metadata updates and the KMS requirement for service principals.

-Dev

--
Dev Patel
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai
From: Rebecca Chan <rebecca.chan@nimbushealth.com>

Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integrating our IdP with your on-prem control plane — questions on failover and provisioning

Thanks — that gives us a good start. A few clarifying items from our platform team after reviewing: 

- For issuer_alias mapping: we can add a custom claim (x-issuer-ref) in our IdP that identifies the origin cluster; is that sufficient for the canonical mapping you described?

- SCIM: our gateway will emit UUID op_ids and cursor headers — we also have a short-lived queue that may re-deliver identical ops after failover. Can Redwood detect duplicate op_ids and ignore replays?

- On break-glass: our security policy prefers group-claim elevation (SAML) since our internal auditors can inspect SAML assertion logs more easily than SCIM provisioning events. Would Redwood's audit stream include raw SAML assertion logs for a given time window?

Let's hold the call until we have a small runbook (1-pager) and the topology PNG you referenced plus mapping CSV so we can walk through it line by line.

—Rebecca

Subject: Re: Integrating our IdP with your on-prem control plane — questions on failover and provisioning

Hi Rebecca / Andrew — attaching a concise runbook and the SCIM mapping CSV you asked for so you can drop it into your internal reviews. A couple extra commitments from our side: 

- We will publish a signed metadata-change API endpoint and require a tenant-level signed request (per Dev's note) — PS: we'll share the API spec before the call.

- Duplicate op_id handling: yes, our SCIM apply loop is idempotent for op_id — duplicates are ignored if the op_id matches a previously applied operation within the retention window (configurable, default 7 days).

- SAML assertion logs: for Private control plane we can export the raw assertion payloads (redacted PII) to your SIEM for a configurable retention window; we will include assertion identifiers and timestamps in the audit stream. Full raw payloads are only available under an NDA for compliance reasons — we can discuss scope.

Proposed next step: 45-min design workshop on Wed 2028-03-07 11:00 PT. I'll send a calendar invite with materials.

Attachments: scim-incremental-mapping.csv, runbook-saml-scim-onprem-1pager.pdf

Best,
Naomi
